topic: Brain freeze: cold palate, brain artery blood surge, tongue fix
hook: Why ice cream gives you brain freeze

slides.title: Cold hits your palate
slides.body: Cold food on the roof of your mouth chills nearby blood vessels.
slides.image_prompt: Melting scoop of blue ice cream in a cone with frost crystals forming around it, cold mist, dark moody background

slides.title: A brain artery swells
slides.body: Blood rushes into a brain artery, and you feel it as pain.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing red network of blood vessels inside a translucent glass brain model, one artery swelling brighter, dark background
slides.credit: Antonino Paolo Di Giovanna (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

slides.title: The quick fix
slides.body: Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth to warm it.
slides.image_prompt: Icy slushie cup beside a small warm glowing ember on a dark table, contrast of cold blue and warm orange light

cta: Follow for a new body fact daily
caption:
That stabbing pain after a fast bite of ice cream has a name: sphenopalatine ganglioneuralgia. In a 2012 study, researchers watched blood flow through a brain artery surge during brain freeze, and the pain faded as the artery narrowed again.

The fix is simple: slow down, or warm the roof of your mouth with your tongue. Save this for your next slushie.

What gives you the worst brain freeze: ice cream, slushies or cold water?
